prompt: What physical quantity is represented by the gradient of a displacement-time graph?

answer.explanation: The gradient of a displacement-time graph is Delta s / Delta t, which represents the rate of change of displacement, defining velocity.

distractor_explanations: Acceleration is the gradient of a velocity-time graph, not a displacement-time graph.
Distance is the path length (scalar), not the rate of change of displacement.
Speed is the gradient of a distance-time graph; because displacement has direction, its gradient gives velocity.
Correct: gradient = Delta s / Delta t = velocity.
hints: Gradient is the change in the vertical quantity divided by the change in time.
Consider the unit: metres divided by seconds gives m s^-1.
solution: D. Gradient = Delta s / Delta t = velocity.
teacher_walkthrough: Here, vertical change is displacement Delta s in metres, horizontal change is time Delta t in seconds.
Delta s / Delta t is the definition of velocity. Therefore D is correct.
